title: Dating a rock by uranium and lead
caption: Starting with no lead, ²³⁸U decays (through a chain) to ²⁰⁶Pb. The fractions cross when half the uranium has gone: equal numbers of parent and daughter mean the rock is one half-life old, 4.5 × 10⁹ years.
alt: Fractions of uranium-238 falling and lead-206 rising with time, crossing at one half at 4.5 billion years.
description: Uranium remaining: 2^(−t/4.5 Gyr). Lead formed: 1 − 2^(−t/4.5 Gyr).
They are equal (D/P = 1) at t = t½ = 4.5 × 10⁹ years.
At two half-lives the ratio D/P is 3, at three it is 7.

checks.name: parent and daughter equal after one half-life
three quarters decayed after two half-lives
